newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds up before US data, prices set to hold.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds up before US data, prices set to hold.

text.p: Danish bond prices continued to rise moderately on Thursday, cheered by the positive Wall Street overnight market ahead of the afternoon's U.S. weekly jobless and June housing starts data, with levels seen holding.
"The 2006 benchmark seems to have hit a technical barrier just below 114 so prices will probably hold at current levels. The market has been more active today," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.12 point up from the start at 113.90, yielding 5.89 percent, with the new seven percent 2007 benchmark 0.16 point higher at 106.70 with yield at 6.10 percent.

Turnover in the 2006 and 2007 benchmarks was 1.8 billion and 630 million crowns respectively. The 2006 benchmark's September future rose 0.33 point to 113.39 with 26 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.10 point to 91.85.
The crown traded at a stable, virtually unchanged 3.8105 per mark at 1115 gmt.
The seven percent 2007's 10-year yield gap with the equivalent German bund widened one basis point to 55.
